page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, running on the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with an AWS Neoverse-V1 processor featuring four physical cores and four vCPUs clocked at 2.6 GHz, providing a dedicated single-threaded core design without hardware multithreading. Cache allocation includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with a bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results show balanced mid-tier execution across primary general-purpose compute metrics. The instance achieves average scores in stress-ng single-core (1532.99) and multi-core (6110.35) tests, as well as Geekbench single-core (1502.0) and multi-core (4871.0) evaluations. It demonstrates competent throughput in Clang software compilation (6328.0), Redis operations (6.71 million SET operations per second), static web serving (8.07 GB/sec), and PassMark database operations (4109.82). Performance dips into lower percentiles on specialized operations, including PassMark encryption (554.37), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (29.46 GB/sec), and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.

The combination of dedicated arm64 compute cores and local NVMe storage provides high density and operational cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from scratch-space I/O. Because the local NVMe drive provides direct attached performance, it avoids network storage overhead for transient files. This server type is best matched with continuous integration build workers, web serving clusters, Redis or Memcached instances with persistent local dump storage, and lightweight relational or document database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized arm64 instance engineered with four physical cores powered by the AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with dedicated single-threaded execution, it features an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory and includes a bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD drive alongside 2 Gbps baseline networking. Synthetic benchmarks indicate consistent median-level throughput across standard compute suites, Clang software compilation, Redis key-value workloads, and static web serving, while showing processing limitations under heavy encryption tests and LLM inference. With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio and fast localized storage, the c7gd.xlarge offers efficient resource utilization for build runners, microservices, caching infrastructure, and low-latency data ingestion.
